flashcards.q: What order does JS run: console.log(1); setTimeout(()=>console.log(2),0); Promise.resolve().then(()=>console.log(3)); console.log(4);?
flashcards.a: 1, 4, 3, 2. Sync code finishes first (1,4). The entire microtask queue drains before the next macrotask (3), then the setTimeout macrotask runs (2).

flashcards.q: What's the event loop rule for microtasks between macrotasks?
flashcards.a: After each single macrotask, the ENTIRE microtask queue drains -- including any new microtasks enqueued during the drain -- before the next macrotask or paint can happen.

flashcards.q: Where does Node's process.nextTick() fit relative to Promise microtasks?
flashcards.a: Higher priority -- Node drains the nextTick queue completely before the Promise microtask queue gets a turn. This is Node-specific, not part of browser semantics.

flashcards.q: Why does `for (var i...) setTimeout(()=>console.log(i))` log the same final value every time?
flashcards.a: var is function-scoped, so all iterations share ONE binding of i. By the time any timeout callback runs (after the loop finishes), i already holds its final value.

flashcards.q: State the four this-binding rules in precedence order.
flashcards.a: new binding > explicit binding (call/apply/bind) > implicit binding (obj.method()) > default binding (undefined in strict mode, global object otherwise). Arrow functions ignore all four -- they lexically capture this from their defining scope and can't be rebound.

flashcards.q: What is the prototype chain and how does `class` relate to it?
flashcards.a: Every object has an internal [[Prototype]] link; property lookup walks own properties then the chain until null. class/extends is sugar that sets up exactly this chain (Dog.prototype.__proto__ = Animal.prototype), not a separate inheritance mechanism.
It walks the object's prototype chain looking for the constructor's .prototype object anywhere in that chain -- it is not a stored type tag.

flashcards.q: Key mechanical differences between ES modules and CommonJS?
flashcards.a: ESM: static resolution, LIVE read-only bindings (imports reflect later source updates), async by spec, supports top-level await. CommonJS: dynamic require() calls, VALUE COPY at require-time, synchronous loading.

When a package is instantiated twice in one dependency tree -- once loaded via require() and once via import -- producing two separate module instances whose instanceof checks and shared state diverge.

flashcards.q: What does await desugar to in terms of the microtask queue?
flashcards.a: await expr is equivalent to Promise.resolve(expr).then(continuation) -- code after await runs as a microtask once that promise settles; async function code runs synchronously up to the first await.

flashcards.q: What's wrong with `await a(); await b();` for two independent async calls, and the fix?
flashcards.a: Sequential await serializes them -- b() doesn't even start until a() resolves, costing total time = a+b instead of max(a,b). Fix: start both first (const pa=a(), pb=b()) then await Promise.all([pa,pb]).

flashcards.q: Difference between Promise.all and Promise.allSettled on rejection?
flashcards.a: Promise.all rejects immediately on the FIRST rejection (others keep running in the background but their results are lost to the caller). Promise.allSettled waits for ALL promises to settle regardless of individual failures.

flashcards.q: What persists across multiple .next() calls on a generator?
flashcards.a: The generator's local execution state (variables, position in the function body) is suspended, not discarded, between calls -- each .next() resumes exactly where the last yield paused.
